questions.q: According to the lesson, what changes about the six quality dimensions (accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness) when applied to training data instead of a report?
options: The consequence of failing them — a training data flaw gets learned as a pattern and applied automatically, without human judgment
The dimensions themselves are completely replaced with new ones for machine learning
The dimensions no longer matter at all once data is used to train a model
Training data is exempt from quality standards entirely
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the same six dimensions still apply — what changes is the severity of the consequence when they fail.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what does a mislabeled training example do, beyond containing one wrong fact?
options: It actively teaches the model the wrong association between an input and an output
It automatically deletes itself from the dataset
It has no effect on the model at all
It only affects the report it originally came from
questions.explain: The lesson explains that mislabeled examples teach incorrect associations, which is a more serious consequence than a single wrong fact in a report.

questions.q: What is 'data leakage,' as defined in the lesson?
options: When the same or related records appear in both training and test data, making test performance look artificially good
When training data is accidentally published on a public website
When a model's code is stolen by a competitor
When a database server runs out of disk space
questions.explain: The lesson defines data leakage specifically as training/test data overlap caused by duplicate or related records, inflating apparent performance.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say timeliness is a particularly tricky quality dimension for training data?
options: A model trained on stale data learns an outdated picture of the world, with no visible warning sign like a report's date stamp
Timeliness only matters for data stored in spreadsheets
Models automatically detect and discard old data on their own
Timeliness is not actually one of the six quality dimensions
questions.explain: The lesson notes that, unlike a dated report, a model gives no visual cue that the patterns it learned may be out of date.

questions.q: What does the lesson mean by ML 'amplifying' rather than just repeating a data quality flaw?
options: A model treats learned patterns as ground truth and extends them confidently and repeatedly to new cases, rather than a human catching the one-off error
ML systems make data files physically larger in storage
ML always doubles the number of rows in a dataset
Amplification only happens when a model is deployed on more than one server
questions.explain: The lesson's core distinction is that a model generalizes and repeats a flaw indefinitely, rather than a human applying skepticism to a single bad data point.
